Confluence

/KON-floo-uhns/ - the stress falls on KON · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Confluence means a flowing together of separate streams, forces, or events into one.

Ask the ranger why the wildflowers exploded this June and she names a confluence — wet winter, cool spring, and last summer's burn.

Worked Example

The city's bike boom traced back to a confluence nobody planned: a gas spike, a new greenway, and a bike-share app that launched the same month. The planners still argue over which mattered most.

Confluence begins as river language — two streams flowing into one channel — and keeps the picture even when nothing is wet: separate forces reaching the same point and moving on together. A coincidence merely happens at once; a confluence combines.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

convergence: Convergence names the approach — separate paths still bending toward one point, a meeting promised but not yet made. A confluence is what convergence becomes at the meeting itself: the joined flow, separate currents now moving on together as one.

junction: A junction is the fixed place where routes meet — a dot on the map, pure geography. A confluence is not a place but a happening: separate streams or forces actually flowing together into one. You can stand at a junction; a confluence carries you along.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

divergence: paths splitting apart from a common point

scattering: elements flung apart, nothing meeting at all

Where it sits · how fully separate things become one — intersection → confluence → fusion

intersection vs. confluence: An intersection stops short of a confluence — the roads touch at one point and go their own ways, each unchanged, while a confluence joins separate streams into one shared flow.

fusion vs. confluence: Fusion goes further than confluence — merged streams still carry two waters in one bed, but fused things have become a single substance with no seam.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together

Root — flu-

Root — flu-: to flow

Suffix — -ence

Suffix — -ence: the state of

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (together) + flu- (to flow) + -ence (the state of) = a flowing together. Latin confluere named the meeting of rivers, and river towns from Koblenz to Pittsburgh still sit on literal confluences. Later use just widens the banks: currents of any kind — money, weather, luck — running into one stream.

Use the root in a new word: fluent

Use the root in a new word: fluent: A fluent speaker's sentences flow on without a single stone in the current.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Reach for confluence when several independent currents arrive together and their combining is the story — rivers, events, causes. A coincidence is mere shared timing; a junction or intersection is just geography. Its unit-mate coalesce is the verb for slowly growing into one; confluence is the noun for the meeting of flows.
